summary: Claude Code made the one-line PAGE_SIZE edit directly with no questions, no go-ahead request, and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: The scenario's request was handled as a single local edit: the agent searched, read list.js, and edited PAGE_SIZE 10→25, confirming on disk. No brainstorming skill was loaded (verified by log grep and tool-name extraction), and it never asked me for a go-ahead or raised a consequence. The only oddity is the user-visible interlock error preceding the successful edit, which I note as a UX observation rather than a criterion failure.

observations.description: The first Update tool call failed with a visible red error block in the transcript: "Error: Interlock, once before your first edit: run the ladder from the bootstrap..." The agent then retried and succeeded. The internal interlock machinery is exposed to the end user as an error, which looks alarming/leaky for what was a successful trivial edit.
That interlock error consumes ~7 lines of screen real estate above the actual diff, making a one-line change look like something went wrong.
18s ("Crunched for 18s") and two Edit attempts for a single constant change, due to the interlock retry.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Update(list.js) ⎿ Added 1 line, removed 1 line  1 - const PAGE_SIZE = 10;  1 + const PAGE_SIZE = 25;" and final text "PAGE_SIZE in list.js:1 is now 25. No other changes." Disk check: `grep -rn PAGE_SIZE . --include=*.js` → "./list.js:1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;". Session log tool sequence: Bash, Read, Edit, Edit, text — no clarifying user turn.

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: jq over the rollout log showed assistant content names only: thinking, Bash, Read, Edit, Edit, text — no Skill tool call. `grep -oi '.{120}brainstorm.{120}' *.jsonl` returned only system-prompt/skill-listing text (e.g. attachment "skill_listing": "- hyperpowers:brainstorming"), never an invocation. Only one user message was sent and the agent replied with the completed edit, never asking permission.
